ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Josephine Baker

code.originalText: Twelve-week review: exercise test, lipids, mood, and the return to performing

text.paragraph: Twelve-week review: exercise test, lipids, mood and the return to performing. [S]

Ms. Baker returns about four months after the heart attack and five weeks after her sick visit for a nosebleed, which has not recurred. She completed all 36 cardiac rehabilitation sessions last week. On the treadmill test today she walked for nine minutes without chest pain or breathlessness. She has been practicing songs and dance steps at home for up to an hour, and she has an offer for a short run of concerts in the autumn. Her home blood pressure averages 122/74. She is sleeping well, her mood is better, and the rehabilitation psychologist helped her with the worry about her family and her debts. She has taken every dose of her medicines. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-07-21; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well and energetic; blood pressure 122/76, pulse 58; weight 60.4 kg

Breathlessness on exertion and tiredness since discharge three weeks after the heart attack, without chest pain at rest; cause to be determined (heart function, ischemia, anemia, medicine effect or deconditioning)
S — Synthetic presenting problem, resolved at the second visit when the echocardiogram and cardiology attributed it to ticagrelor.

Coronary artery disease after a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction three weeks before intake, treated with one drug-eluting stent to the right coronary artery; synthetic modern episode linked to the documented heart attack of March 1969
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the 1969 heart attack remains D in the history.
High blood pressure, found during the hospital stay for the heart attack
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; no claim about her real blood pressure.

Absence of the uterus after an emergency hysterectomy at about 35, during a long, grave illness after the loss of a pregnancy; whether the ovaries were removed is not known; counted as a possible early menopause when weighing her cardiovascular risk
S — Synthetic modern status linked to the retrospective account of a hysterectomy in 1941 or 1942; the operation itself rests on one secondary source.
Breathlessness from ticagrelor: a common, harmless side effect, resolved after the change to clopidogrel
S — Synthetic diagnosis at the second visit; resolved at the third visit after the switch.
Raised lipoprotein(a), 172 nmol/L, an inherited risk-enhancing factor
S — Synthetic result measured once at the second visit.
Financial strain: heavy debts after the loss of her home and estate, with income only from performing, which she has stopped while she recovers
S — Synthetic social need anchored to her documented debts and the loss of Les Milandes.
Anterior nosebleed from the left side of the nose, lasting about 25 minutes, in dry weather on aspirin and clopidogrel; stopped with pressure; no further bleeding
S — Synthetic intercurrent problem at an unscheduled visit; it follows from dual antiplatelet therapy and does not echo a documented illness.

list.item:
Coronary artery disease after a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (I25.10). No angina; exercise capacity about 10 METs with no ischemia on the test, which is enough for stage performance. LDL 62 mg/dL, a 58% fall from 146, below the 70 mg/dL goal; ezetimibe not needed. Seattle Angina Questionnaire-7 94. [S]
Graded return to the stage: rehearsals at the effort reached in rehabilitation first, then full performances, with rest between shows, water, and nitroglycerin in the dressing room.
Continue dual antiplatelet therapy to twelve months, atorvastatin 80 mg and metoprolol.
Exercise most days: brisk walking or dance practice, 150 minutes a week or more.

High blood pressure (I10). At goal, 122/76; metoprolol will continue beyond the first year because of high blood pressure. [S]
No change.

Mood after the heart attack. PHQ-9 3 from 7: minimal symptoms with rehabilitation and its psychologist; no thoughts of self-harm. [S]
PHQ-2 at the preventive visit; repeat PHQ-9 if it rises.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes (2025); Depression and Coronary Heart Disease: Recommendations for Screening, Referral, and Treatment: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association (2008); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, ischemic heart disease and acute myocardial infarction monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Preventive visit in about eight weeks. Seven-month review in about three months with a metabolic panel and a blood count. Call 911 for chest pain not relieved five minutes after one nitroglycerin. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-15: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
